sri: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — I ran a small sim comparing inflight aggregation with per-tenant pinning. Wanted to surface a few surprising tradeoffs and get thoughts on headroom sizing.

 dave: Nice. Any numbers?

 sri: short summary: with strict pinning we saw tail p99 latency improve for high-QPS tenants but overall throughput drops ~6% when headroom < 15%. With looser aggregation (time-based windows) throughput is better but some tenants hit higher variance.

 maya: Interesting. Is throughput drop due to underutilized slots or increased eviction churn?

 sri: mostly eviction churn + wasted KV cache warmup. Pinning prevents good coalescing of compatible requests, so GPUs have smaller batches and more frequent kernel launches.

 dave: That matches my local perf runs. Also saw that per-tenant pinning amplifies cold-starts when model variants switch (quantized vs fp16) because caches don't carry across pinned islands.

 jen: Could we try soft-pinning? e.g., prefer pinning for tenants above some sustained QPS for N seconds, but allow preemption if headroom falls below threshold.

 maya: Soft-pinning sounds promising. Two quick controls I'd add: 1) age-based decay so old inflight tokens can be merged after X ms, 2) weight-based admission using tenant priority to decide preemption order.

 dave: +1. Also add an admission metric: inflight_headroom = reserved_slots - sum(pinned_slots) per GPU. If inflight_headroom < low_watermark, trigger deferred coalesce.

 sri: I'm worried about oscillation: tenants repeatedly pinned/unpinned leading to constant rebalancing. How to bound that?

 jen: hysteresis and cooldown windows. e.g., pin only if sustained for T_pin and unpin only after T_unpin without meeting criteria. Also track a pin_count and cap changes per-minute.

 maya: Another angle: make pinning decisions at shard-level instead of GPU-level so multiple GPUs can collaborate. Helps when single-GPU bins are overloaded. But requires cross-GPU coordination signals.

 dave: Cross-GPU coordination adds complexity and extra RPCs. Might be okay if we piggyback on existing placement heartbeats. Need telemetry to prove benefit.

 sri: For the RFC follow-up, I'll prototype soft-pinning + decay + hysteresis and run sim with realistic tenant mix. Any additional telemetry to add to the sim?

 dave: track: paxos-style? jk. Seriously: measure batch size distribution per-tenant, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kernel_launch_rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies per-tenant, and preemption_count.

 maya: Also record reaggregation_delay (time between when a request could be coalesced and when it actually was) and eviction_warmup_tokens ratio.

 deploy-bot: perf-sim-run-187 finished: sim v3, 15k tenants, 24h workload. Results uploaded to: https://redwood-internal/sims/187

 sri: sweet — I'll grab the run and post a short writeup. Plan: prototype in the sim, then small canary on staging with a single GPU pool and observability flags. If staging looks good, roll to more pools with conservative defaults.

 jen: Sounds good. If the sim shows >4% throughput regression for default headroom, we should prefer aggregation-first defaults and make pinning opt-in per-customer.

 dave: Agreed. One more ask: add a debug endpoint that returns current pin map + recent pin events for a tenant to make troubleshooting easier.

 sri: will do. Thanks all. Will post follow-up with sim graphs and config knobs later today. :+1:
